formula_checks.name: isBond
formula_checks.why: One definition — the account's class — as owner DEC-0343 requires and as the spec quoted on the card says. Whether a maturity-dated CD is a bond then rests on assetClassOf's order (judged in networth 02: maturity date should come before name evidence).
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0343; spec §2 quoted on the card.

formula_checks.name: itemising
formula_checks.why: Keep-total = entered balance, itemised = Σ listed values, remainder = the difference — the three figures the screen needs, and the total never moves. A negative remainder honestly shows over-itemising. Keep full precision and round only at display, so 0.10 + 0.20 against 0.30 shows $0, not −$0.
formula_checks.rests_on: Formula in words; Itemising type ('its total never moves'); owner DEC-0264.

formula_checks.name: ledgerGroups
formula_checks.why: It counts every account WHOLE under one class, while the class rows above it (assetAllocation) split a linked account by its breakdown. Two formulas describe the same thing differently: in the approved drawing the ledger's Cash group is $8,000 while the WHAT YOU OWN Cash row is $8,838, and Stocks is $349,333 against $348,495. By institution, Vanguard's mix shows one kind ($349,333 stocks), so the 'what is inside this institution' line (MK-NW-M-063) is left out though it holds cash and stocks. Also: institution names are grouped by exact text, so 'Fidelity' and 'fidelity ' become two groups.
formula_checks.should_be: Group totals and the institution mix use the same split as the class rows: a linked account contributes each breakdown slice to its class (its row can sit under its main class with its split shown). Institution names are compared trimmed and with capitals ignored. Invariant: by-class group totals = assetAllocation; by-class and by-institution grand totals equal.
formula_checks.rests_on: Approved drawing 'Net worth, Quiet Instrument v08, state A'; owner DEC-0343; owner DEC-0069 (By institution matches By category); author rule on M-006 (switching view can never change what you own).

formula_checks.name: alternativesSummary
formula_checks.why: Growth in a year is 0 when there is no rate (nothing held). The AltSummary type says 'Null when nothing is held: 0% would read as a forecast' for the rate, and MK-NW-M-050 refuses the growth figure for the same reason; a $0 growth is the same false forecast. The rest is right, and isAlternative now uses assetClassOf, so the total matches the Net worth Alternatives slice for hand-entered accounts.
formula_checks.should_be: Growth in a year = total × blended rate, and no figure (null) when nothing is held or the total is 0.
formula_checks.rests_on: AltSummary type comment; refusal rule of MK-NW-M-050.

formula_checks.name: incomeBearingClassOf
formula_checks.why: Silent on whether words match as whole words or anywhere in the name — which decides real cases: 'Putnam Large Cap Value Fund' contains 'put', 'Callaway Golf Co' contains 'call' and 'gold', 'ABCD Industries' contains 'cd', 'Treasury Wine Estates' is a company. 'Unless the name is a company's' is not defined. And the first rule (sweep/settlement → cash) collides with owner DEC-0051/0309 when the settlement vehicle is itself a money-market fund ('Vanguard Federal Money Market Fund — settlement fund'): one owner rule says cash, the other Stocks / Funds.
formula_checks.should_be: Match words and tickers as whole tokens, capitals ignored; define the company test (e.g. Inc/Corp/Co/Ltd/plc or a listed equity ticker → no commodity/currency evidence); owner to rule on a money-market settlement fund.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0051, DEC-0092, DEC-0309; founder rule 2026-08-04 on the card.

formula_checks.name: realEstateUseOf
formula_checks.why: Any property with no use stated becomes the primary home. A household with a home and a let condo, neither marked, gets two primary homes; the rental then takes the 0% retirement earmark (earmarkDefault) and drops out of the nest egg. A default invented where the honest answer is 'not stated'.
formula_checks.should_be: The stated use; when none is stated, primary only if it is the household's only real-estate account; otherwise no answer, and the screen asks.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief: no invented defaults; earmarkDefault (MK-NW-F-030) uses this answer.

formula_checks.name: isRealAsset
formula_checks.why: Real estate or personal property by the one class function — the definition investableAssets relies on.

formula_checks.name: totalAssets
formula_checks.why: 'A missing balance counts as zero' — a linked account not yet synced, or a home whose value was never typed, silently lowers What you own and Net worth with nothing on screen to say so. The sum of known balances is the right number, but it must not pass as the whole.
formula_checks.should_be: Σ known balances, plus a count of accounts with no value, which the screen states ('1 account has no value yet'); never presented as complete while that count is above zero.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief: 'something missing counted as zero'; owner DEC-0061 (missing-data banner).

formula_checks.name: equitiesTotal
formula_checks.why: Counts a linked account whole under its one class, while assetAllocation (MK-NW-F-029) splits it — two formulas for the same Stocks / Funds figure. The approved drawing's Vanguard counts $349,333 here against $348,495 on the class row; a linked Schwab account holding a T-bill and cash puts both inside 'equities'.
formula_checks.should_be: equitiesTotal = assetAllocation's Stocks / Funds value (linked accounts by breakdown slice).
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0343 (one concept, one function; a total and its parts pinned by invariant); approved drawing state A.

formula_checks.name: fixedIncomeTotal
formula_checks.why: Same fault as equitiesTotal: a T-bill or CD held inside a linked brokerage (class Stocks / Funds) is left out entirely, though the class row and the Bonds screen count it.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0343; owner DEC-0051 (CDs/T-bills → Bonds & CDs).

formula_checks.name: alternativesTotal
formula_checks.why: Options inside a linked brokerage are Alternatives in the breakdown and on the Net worth class row, but this total counts only whole accounts classed Alternatives, so it misses them — and the author's rule on MK-NW-M-049 says the Alternatives total must equal the Net worth tab's slice.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0343; author rule on MK-NW-M-049.

formula_checks.name: realEstateTotal
formula_checks.why: Real estate is never split out of a linked brokerage (a REIT fund is Stocks / Funds), so whole-account counting agrees with assetAllocation here.

formula_checks.name: accountLastFour
formula_checks.why: 'From the mask, or failing that its account number' does not say what 'failing' means when a mask exists but has fewer than four digits ('••21'): fall back to the account number, or give nothing.
formula_checks.should_be: Use the mask when it yields four or more digits; otherwise the account number when it yields four or more; otherwise nothing.
formula_checks.rests_on: The card's purpose ('null when we genuinely don't have them').

formula_checks.name: accountDisplayName
formula_checks.why: For an account at a named institution that is not tax-advantaged but has digits, the kind word is dropped: Chase checking ••4821 and Chase savings ••9930 read 'Chase -4821' and 'Chase -9930', so a person cannot tell which is savings. Owner DEC-0406: always be explicit. Also, with an institution set the person's own label is never shown.
formula_checks.should_be: With an institution: Institution + kind word + -last four for every account that has a kind word (digits left out when unknown); Institution -last four only when there is no kind word.

formula_checks.name: blendedVolatility
formula_checks.why: A value-weighted AVERAGE of volatilities is not a portfolio's volatility: it ignores how the parts move together and equals the true figure only when every part moves in lockstep. Half stocks (16%) and half bonds (6%) averages to 11%; with the long-run stock–bond correlation of about 0.2 the portfolio is about 9.1%. The overstated risk feeds the range of outcomes in the retirement odds. And '12% when nothing is earmarked' is an invented number.
formula_checks.should_be: Portfolio volatility = √(Σᵢ Σⱼ wᵢ wⱼ σᵢ σⱼ ρᵢⱼ), weights = earmarked shares, with a stated correlation table by class (cash at 0 volatility). No answer when nothing is earmarked.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard portfolio-variance formula (Markowitz mean–variance); brief: no invented defaults.
